title: Eager Copying of Reference Parameters (Unnecessary Ownership Request)
pattern: A function accepts a reference parameter (`&T` or `&str`) and immediately clones or converts it to an owned type (`T` or `String`).
why_bad: It forces a costly heap allocation and memory copy on every call, even when the caller might already own a temporary value that they could have passed directly, losing allocator control and upfront visibility of costs.
detection: Look for parameters taken by reference (`&String`, `&Vec<T>`, `&[T]`) that are cloned immediately in the function body without semantic mutation of the underlying shared structure.
counterexample: The function only needs to own the data conditionally under rare branches (e.g., error recovery, logging, dynamic format changes). `Context-dependent`.
fix: Change the function signature to take an owned value (`String` or `Vec<T>`) or use `std::borrow::Cow` to defer allocation only when modification is needed.
